constraints.text: Do not add spoken or sung lines.

description.text: At the very first instant the frame is the complete supplied character reference sheet, reproduced in a watercolour storybook rendering: a tall vertical layout with a large cinematic hero panel across the top, three full-body turnaround figures in the middle row, and four close detail crops along the bottom, all separated by thin dividers. In the hero panel a woman in a black high-collared jacket, dark cargo trousers and black lace-up combat boots stands centered on a wet bridge at night, arms relaxed at her sides, head turned slightly toward the left, with short dark hair, a diagonal scar through one eyebrow, and rain streaking past glowing streetlamps, metal railings and dark building facades mirrored in the wet pavement. The turnaround row shows the same figure front, in side profile and from behind against a dark neutral studio background, while the bottom row isolates her face, the strapped and buckled jacket collar, her two hands, and her laced boots. Every panel, divider and existing label - HERO, FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, BACK, FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS and BOOTS - stays fixed in its original place. The whole sheet then begins a slow, even visual dissolve, the painted watercolour edges softly loosening as the image is carried toward the second sheet, with no pan, zoom, crop or rearrangement of any panel.
The entire first reference sheet sits in the frame unchanged, its rainy night hero panel, turnaround row, detail crops and labels all intact.
A slow, even dissolve starts to soften the sheet's watercolour surface while every panel and label holds its position.

The shot transitions to the continuing slow dissolve, the character sheet fading out evenly as the second reference sheet fades in, both surfaces briefly overlapping as pale, blooming watercolour washes. What resolves is the complete supplied dragon reference sheet in the same painted storybook treatment: a wide volcanic hero view across the top and six smaller labeled panels arranged in two rows beneath, divided by thin lines. In the hero view a massive black dragon crouches on four legs with its dark membranous wings spread wide, its long horned head lowered, its tail sweeping behind it, one glowing orange eye catching the light; multiple pale horns rise from its skull, and overlapping scales carry a faint blue-gray sheen against rocky mountains, drifting smoke and mist, reflective wet ground and scattered glowing orange patches. The panels below show the creature front on, in side profile, from the rear, in a head close view, plus a wing membrane study with finger-like struts, a curved-clawed foot and a scale detail. At the final instant the frame is exactly the second sheet, uncropped and unmoved, with all of its existing labels and dividers in their original positions.
The first sheet continues fading as the second sheet emerges through the dissolve.
The dissolve nearly completes, leaving the dragon sheet crisp, with its hero view, six panels, labels and dividers in place.

summary.text: A slow visual dissolve carries the first supplied character reference sheet into the second supplied dragon reference sheet, holding both complete endpoint frames exactly at the start and the end.

claims.text: The video must begin on the first supplied picture exactly and end on the second supplied picture exactly, with a slow visual dissolve between them and the complete pixels of both endpoint pictures preserved.
No spoken or sung lines are to be added.
The first image is a multi-panel character reference sheet with a rainy night hero panel, FRONT, SIDE PROFILE and BACK turnaround views, and FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS and BOOTS detail crops.
The second image is a dragon reference sheet with a wide volcanic hero view and FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, REAR, HEAD CLOSE, WING MEMBRANE, CLAW AND FOOT and SCALE DETAIL panels.
